description: A composite figure group consisting of one data table plus a multi-panel XRD study of a mechanically alloyed high-entropy steel powder. The standalone table lists 15 binary alloy pairs (Fe-Mn, Fe-Ni, Fe-Al, Fe-Si, Fe-C, Mn-Ni, Mn-Al, Mn-Si, Mn-C, Ni-Al, Ni-Si, Ni-C, Al-Si, Al-C, Si-C) with binary mixing enthalpy (kJ/mol) and liquidus temperature (C), ranging from 1 kJ/mol / 1420 C for Fe-Mn to -60 kJ/mol for Fe-C and 2100 C for Al-C and Si-C; these values feed a machine-learning/semi-empirical Miedema estimate of the alloy melting point. Panel (a) stacks XRD patterns of the milled powder at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 h, intensity (a.u.) versus 2theta (Degree) from 20 to 100, with a symbol legend for elements (#Fe, ∇Mn, ΔNi, ●Al, ♦Si, ★C) and phases (♥BCC, ♣gamma-brass type, ◇B2-type). Panel (b) is an enlarged view over 2theta = 49-54. Panel (c) is the 35 h pattern over 2theta = 30-100 with reflections labelled (110), (411), (100), (332), (200), (211). The inset (d) is the Rietveld refinement of the 35 h powder, showing Obs, Calc, Bkg, Zero and phase contributions over 2theta = 20-120. Together they document progressive alloying, disappearance of elemental peaks and formation of a multi-phase structure.

subfigures.description: Tabular data listing 15 binary alloys (Fe-Mn through Si-C) with columns 'Binary Alloys', 'Binary Enthalpy (kJ/mol)' and 'Liquidus Temperature (°C)'; values run from +1 kJ/mol / 1420 °C (Fe-Mn) to -60 kJ/mol (Fe-C) and 2100 °C (Al-C, Si-C).

Stacked XRD patterns of milled Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 powder at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 h of milling, plotted as Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (Degree) over 20-100°. Element markers (#Fe, ∇Mn, ΔNi, ●Al, ♦Si, ★C) fade with milling time while phase markers (♥BCC, ♣γ-brass type, ◇B2-type) appear and grow.
Enlarged view of the same stacked patterns restricted to 2θ = 49-54°, showing the (110)-region peaks with ♥BCC, ♣γ-brass type, ◇B2-type and # markers; the BCC reflection dominates at 25-35 h.

Single XRD pattern of the 35 h milled sample, Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (Degree) over 30-100°, labelled with (100), (110), (411) for γ-brass/B2/BCC region and (332), (200), (211) at higher angles, with legend ♥BCC, ◇B2-type, ♣γ-brass type, ♦Si.

Inset Rietveld refinement plot of the 35 h milled powder: observed (Obs) and calculated (Calc) profiles, background (Bkg), zero line and Bragg-position rows for BCC, γ-brass type, B2 type and Si, plotted over 2θ = 20-120° with a difference curve.

observations.observation: The table lists 15 binary alloy pairs with binary mixing enthalpy (kJ/mol) and liquidus temperature (°C) for computing the melting point of the high entropy steel.
In the table, Fe-Mn has the only positive binary enthalpy (+1 kJ/mol) with a liquidus temperature of 1420 °C, while Fe-C has the most negative enthalpy (-60 kJ/mol).
Al-C and Si-C both list the highest liquidus temperature in the table, 2100 °C, with binary enthalpies of -13 and -4 kJ/mol respectively.
Panel (a) stacks XRD patterns recorded after 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 h of milling, plotted as Intensity (a.u.) against 2θ (Degree) from 20 to 100.
The panel (a) legend assigns # to Fe, ∇ to Mn, Δ to Ni, ● to Al, ♦ to Si and ★ to C, and assigns ♥ to BCC, ♣ to γ-brass type and ◇ to B2-type.
Diffraction peak intensities of all the elemental constituents decrease with milling time, and the low-intensity element peaks have vanished after 5 h of milling.
After 25 h of milling a solid solution forms, consisting of BCC (a = 0.286 nm; JCPDS# 00-006-0696) and γ-brass type (a = 0.872 nm; JCPDS# 01-078-2831) structures, as stated in the text.
Panel (b) zooms the 2θ = 49-54° range and shows the main BCC (♥) reflection together with γ-brass type (♣), B2-type (◇) and #-marked peaks in the stacked 0-35 h patterns.
Panel (c) shows the 35 h milled powder with indexed reflections labelled (100), (110), (411), (332), (200) and (211), and is annotated '35 h'.

Inset (d) presents the Rietveld refinement of the 35 h milled sample with observed, calculated, background and zero curves plus Bragg-position ticks for BCC, γ-brass type, B2 type and Si over 2θ = 20-120°.
The BCC phase is a major phase after 35 h of milling, coexisting with γ-brass type and B2-type (a = 0.290 nm; JCPDS# 01-083-3994) phases plus a trace amount of Si.
Peak broadening and decreasing diffraction-peak intensity with milling are attributed to lattice distortion, induced lattice strain and grain refinement.
